picks.file: Malaga - 1578 views of Sevilla, Cadiz and Malaga (cropped).jpg
picks.what: View from the sea, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: colored Málaga strip of the 1572 Seville–Cádiz–Málaga plate; Gibralfaro, the Alcazaba and the harbor; border cut

picks.file: Gezicht op Malaga vanuit het Noorden, RP-T-1953-291.jpg
picks.what: View over the city and the cathedral, watercolor (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: color, dated June 1836; cathedral, beach and mountains unmistakable

picks.file: Gezicht op Málaga, met op de achtergrond de Kathedraal VUE DE MALAGA & DE LA CATHÉDRALE (titel op object), RP-F-F07610.jpg
picks.what: The cathedral and Gibralfaro over the rooftops, stereo photograph (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: trimmed to the left half of the stereo card; cathedral and castle hill both in view; Rijksmuseum dates it 1862–76

picks.file: View of the Port of Málaga c1961.jpg
picks.what: The bullring and the port from Gibralfaro, photograph (U.S. Navy)
picks.why: only general view for the 20th century; bullring, lighthouse and harbor recognizable

picks.file: Vista de Málaga desde el castillo de Gibralfaro, España, 2023-05-20, DD 113.jpg
picks.what: View from Gibralfaro Castle over the Alcazaba, the port and the cathedral, photograph
picks.why: high-resolution modern view with the Alcazaba, cathedral and harbor; tree foreground trimmed

gaps: P0: nothing; P2: only copies of the 1572 view (#9, #10), skipped
notes: #1, #4, #5, #7 are Vélez-Málaga, a different town. #14–#16 are Bécquer paintings of Seville held in the Carmen Thyssen museum in Málaga. #9 (1657, Janssonius) and #10 (about 1700, van den Berge) re-engrave the 1572 Braun and Hogenberg view. #12 (Laborde, 1812) is a good black-and-white alternative for P3. #17 (Laurent) is low-resolution and only loosely dated. #24 (1900s postcard of the bullring and port) would fill the early 20th century but is too close in date to #21 for a second P4.
